key_insight: InterMimicGen turns sparse human-object interaction data into scalable humanoid loco-manipulation training by making motion data and the imitation policy co-improve each other. The key breakthrough is a self-evolving loop that continually expands usable robot motion supervision.
problem_solved: Humanoid loco-manipulation is hard to train because real human-object interaction data are limited, diverse, and not directly executable on robots. This paper addresses the gap between rich human demonstrations and robot-ready whole-body control.
method: Consolidate multiple motion-captured human-object interaction datasets into a unified source of demonstrations.
Retarget human motions to humanoid robot references while preserving whole-body coordination and hand-object interaction details.
Use a self-evolving pipeline where robot motion data and a tracking policy iteratively improve each other, scaling imitation training over time.
impact: This matters because it provides a practical way to scale humanoid manipulation learning without relying on large amounts of hand-collected robot data. For practitioners, it suggests a reusable framework for turning heterogeneous human demonstrations into stronger robot policies.
visual_elements: A left-to-right pipeline showing human motion capture data being retargeted to humanoid robot references.

paper_title: InterMimicGen: Scaling Humanoid Loco-Manipulation through Self-Evolving Motion Imitation
paper_authors: Yucheng Zhang, Sirui Xu, Jinhong Li, Liuyu Bian, Anatulya Nandi
